work_or_witness: Root: A Game of Woodland Might and Right · A Game of Woodland Might and Right
definition: The fantastic forest kingdom and wilderness contested by Root's player factions.
cultural_caution: A fictional setting, not a real forest, territory, or Indigenous homeland.

citations.locator: A Game of Woodland Might and Right
supports: Describes the Woodland as the contested setting.

work_or_witness: Root: A Game of Woodland Might and Right · The Marquise de Cat
definition: One base-game faction board/system, described as an engine-building and logistics game that produces buildings and crafts.
cultural_caution: A player faction title, not a stable individual character or an endorsement of monarchy/extraction.

supports: Defines the faction's base-game play system.

work_or_witness: Root: A Game of Woodland Might and Right · The Eyrie Dynasties
definition: One base-game faction board/system that musters hawks, captures territory, and builds roosts before collapsing into squabbling.
cultural_caution: A collective game system; its bird imagery and dynastic language do not make a single individual character.

supports: Defines the faction's base-game play system.

work_or_witness: Root: A Game of Woodland Might and Right · The Woodland Alliance
definition: One base-game faction board/system that recruits forces and conspiracies, builds late-game presence, and seeks to keep other players in check.
cultural_caution: A fictional insurgency-style game system. Avoid mapping it directly to any real resistance movement or political cause.

supports: Defines the faction's base-game play system.

work_or_witness: Root: A Game of Woodland Might and Right · The Vagabond
definition: A base-game player role that plays all sides of the conflict, explores, fights factions, and pursues a hidden goal.
cultural_caution: A variable player role with character cards, not a fixed named individual or a description of unhoused people.

supports: Defines Vagabond play in the base game.

work_or_witness: Root: A Game of Woodland Might and Right · 2. Key Concepts; 2.1 Cards; Glossary references
definition: Board locations used in Root's faction and card procedures; the Law identifies cards by bird, fox, rabbit, or mouse suit and uses clearings in rules resolution.
cultural_caution: Map spaces and rules objects, not real locations or character nodes.

supports: Uses clearings and suits in the game's core rules structure.

work_or_witness: Root: A Game of Woodland Might and Right · 2.1 Cards
definition: A card-related game procedure: most shared-deck cards have an effect that a player can craft.
cultural_caution: A rules procedure rather than a character vocation, artifact biography, or real craft tradition.

supports: States that most cards have an effect players can craft.

work_or_witness: Root: A Game of Woodland Might and Right · The New Alliance
definition: A Woodland Alliance token system: one token per clearing, with placement as a primary way to gain victory points and later revolts possible in sympathetic regions.
cultural_caution: A source-specific board-game term. It should not be reduced to real political support or emotional empathy.

supports: Explains sympathy tokens, placement, victory points, and revolts during base-game development.

work_or_witness: Root: A Game of Woodland Might and Right · Squires and Disciples deck description
definition: A Root rules concept expressly subject to later deck effects; it is retained as a game-mechanics term but not elaborated from a later printing in this first-printing audit.
cultural_caution: A game victory/rules concept, not support for real domination or political hierarchy.

supports: Identifies dominance as a Root game concept affected by a later optional deck.

work_or_witness: Root: A Game of Woodland Might and Right · 1.4.1 Turn Structure
definition: The three phases of a player's turn in the current Law of Root.
cultural_caution: Turn-phase labels; current Law wording is a later rules witness and is not treated as proof that first-printing wording was identical.

supports: Defines the three turn phases in the current Law.
